note: A 25-page HF-propagation modelling paper whose exhibit set is balanced between drawings and plots: five schematics (the hop, the two-peak terrain, the boat, the curved-earth model and the ionospheric fan), five line plots, one bar chart and exactly one three-dimensional surface. Every caption prints below its artwork, numbering is 'Figure N' except at both ends of the paper where the number is glued to the word ('Figure1', 'Figure6'), and one figure is cited in roman numerals as 'Figure VI'. Reference hygiene is the weak point: Figure 9 is only ever cited as 'Figure 8', Figure 6 is announced as one schematic and captioned as another, and Figures 11 and 12 are announced together by the plural deictic 'as shown in the following figures'. The only table is an uncaptioned, unnumbered two-column notation glossary whose verticals are the paper's only vertical rules. Five measured regions are display equations pasted as MathType images rather than exhibits, and the paper's most ambitious figure - the MATLAB sea surface - prints with no axis titles and no colour scale.
rules: All twelve figure captions print BELOW their artwork and not one prints above, so this paper sits with the below-caption majority of the lane at every page of the body [caption.position].

The numbering glues the number to the title at both ends of the paper - 'Figure1' on p5 and 'Figure6' on p15 - and spaces it in the ten between, so the paper uses two numbering forms for one run of twelve [caption.numbering].

Captions are 4 to 10 words, almost all bare noun phrases ('Wave spectrum', 'Loss comparison chart', 'Boat and antenna schematic'), and not one names a unit, a variable or a condition or states a result [caption.words].

One caption slot carries a prose sentence as well as the title: 'Figure 3 is our simulation of the waves.' prints above the printed caption, so the same figure is announced, titled and captioned in three consecutive lines [caption.verbatim].
One caption misspells its own subject and prints that way: 'Double-edged peak diffration' for diffraction, on the same line as the glued number 'Figure6' [caption.words].

One figure is cited in roman numerals three pages after its arabic citation: 'Figure 6 is a schematic of the Epstein-Peterson method' on p14 against 'The meaning of the parameters in the formula refer to Figure VI' on p15 [mention.style].

Figure 9 is never cited by its own number: the only sentence printed under its caption says 'shown in Figure 8[15]', which is the same sentence already used for Figure 8 a page earlier, so two consecutive schematics share one reference [mention.style].

A figure is announced as one thing and captioned as another: p14 calls Figure 6 a schematic of the Epstein-Peterson method while its caption reads 'Double-edged peak diffration' [mention.lead_sentence].

References split into a subject-first grammar ('Figure 4 describes', 'Figure 5 shows', 'Figure 6 is') and a passive one ('as shown in Figure 7', 'shown in Figure 10'), with two exhibits - Figures 11 and 12 - announced only by the plural deictic 'as shown in the following figures' [mention.lead_pattern].

Three references displace by exactly one page - Figure 2 cited on p8 for p9, Figure 6 cited on p14 for p15, and Figure 12 announced on p20 inside the plural 'following figures' for p21 - and the other nine are local, so the paper never displaces a reference by more than one page [mention.lead_pages].
The exhibit inventory is 5 schematics, 5 line plots, 1 bar chart and 1 surface, so drawings and plots are balanced and neither form dominates [geometry.family].
Exactly one exhibit is three-dimensional: Figure 3's sea surface, flat-shaded and colour-coded by height with no wireframe and no colour scale, printed as a perspective box [geometry.three_d].
The only colour scale in the paper is that unlabelled height shading - no exhibit carries a colourbar, so the surface's colours are decorative rather than readable [geometry.colorbar].

Legends appear on five of the twelve figures and never outside the plot except on the sensitivity pair: inside at upper right on Figures 2, 4 and 5, and outside-right on Figures 11 and 12 where the twelve-entry box overflows the frame [geometry.legend].

The sensitivity pair fails at exactly the point where the legend matters: Figure 11's legend lists twelve series from t=0 to t=22 while only two traces can be told apart, so the key cannot be matched to the ink [geometry.legend].

Figure 12's y axis has no usable scale - ticks from 1.6582 to 1.6586 printed to four decimals on a step near 0.00006 make adjacent labels identical - while its partner Figure 11 prints a coarse -10 to 50 axis, so a caller comparing them compares a readable and an unreadable ordinand [geometry.printed_numbers].

The four drawn schematics and the two terrain drawings carry no numbers at all, and only Figure 6 prints axis words ('height', 'distance'), so in this paper a schematic is identified by its absence of scale rather than by its content [geometry.printed_numbers].

Five of the twelve carry a printed in-frame title above the plot as well as a caption below it, and the two disagree often enough to matter: Figure 5's frame names a frequency curve, its caption names a reflection coefficient and the sentence above it names a roughness factor [geometry.data_labels].

The single grid is the notation glossary on p4: two columns, fifteen rows, announced by a sentence that ends in a colon and followed by no label at all, so the paper's only table is also its only unnumbered exhibit [mention.lead_pattern].

The glossary's rule style is the paper's only one - rules above and below the header and a closing rule at the foot, with a single vertical rule between the symbol and definition columns and no side rules - so the grid is booktabs plus one internal vertical [table.rule_style].

No shading, no merged cell, no two-tier header, no unit in the header, no note line and no continuation: the glossary is as plain as a grid can be, and the italic symbol column is the only typographic signal in the paper's tables [table.zebra].

Five of the eighteen measured regions are not exhibits at all but MathType display equations pasted as graphics (11 and 12 on p8, 18 to 20 on p12), so the region detector counts inline mathematics as artwork on this paper [place.doc_order].

Exhibit size runs the other way from importance: the notation glossary at 0.29 of a page is the largest object in the paper, the twelve figures run 0.086 to 0.21, and the only three-dimensional exhibit, the surface, is the third smallest at 0.10 [place.area_frac].

Seven of the twelve figures print in the top third of their page and only one prints in the bottom third - Figure 3, the surface - so the page rhythm is a figure at the head followed by its discussion below it [place.page_zone].
